disclaimer: Educational decision support only. Similar symptoms can have non-disease causes. Confirm diagnosis with a KVK, agricultural extension officer, or plant pathologist. Use only products registered for the crop and disease locally and follow the current label.

symptoms: Oval purple-brown concentric lesions with yellow margins
Leaves and seed stalks bend and dry
prevention: Use healthy seed, rotate, and remove residue
Improve spacing and avoid late overhead irrigation
treatment: Use a registered fungicide with local guidance
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Pale elongated leaf patches develop grey-violet fuzzy growth
prevention: Improve airflow and minimize long leaf-wetness periods
treatment: Remove infected plants and improve drying
Use a registered anti-oomycete product based on local forecasting
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Small yellow to brown lesions enlarge along one side of leaves
Lesions turn dark and leaves collapse
prevention: Control thrips injury and remove residue
Use balanced nutrition and reduce leaf wetness
treatment: Use a registered fungicide only after confirmation
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Leaves yellow and die from tips
Roots rot and basal plate becomes brown; bulbs may rot in storage
prevention: Use resistant varieties and clean sets
Rotate, avoid wounds, and store bulbs cool and dry
treatment: No dependable cure; improve rotation, sanitation, and storage
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Plants yellow and collapse in patches
White fluffy growth and tiny black sclerotia form at bulb bases
prevention: Use clean planting material and equipment
Do not move contaminated soil; use long rotations and local sanitation measures
treatment: Remove affected plants with surrounding soil carefully
Seek specialist soil-treatment and quarantine advice
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Neck or inner scales become water-soaked and soft
Bulbs collapse and may smell foul
prevention: Avoid wounds and harvest in dry weather
Cure bulbs fully and keep stores cool, dry, and ventilated
treatment: Discard rotting bulbs and sanitize storage areas
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails
